paragraphs: Hattosepet shel nr"n dibchinat layla, kebar bearnu meqom qabbalatam; veatta nebaer meqom tosepet nepesh rucha neshama (nr"n) shel hayyom, shehem meullim ugedolim min hallayla, vehu: baamirat "nishmat kol chay" tekavven lehakin atzmeka leqabbel atta tosepet nepesh shel hayyom. gam tzarik shettekavven berashe tebot "nishmat kol chay" oleh mispar shelosha hvyv"t; vegam tekavven: "kol chay" oleh mispar hy"h yhv"h hy"h, vehem mispar "chayyim"; vekavvanot ellu hem temurat hattepillin, ki hem sod hattepillin hanniqraim "chayye hammelek", ukemo shekkatub bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l. vekatab harab morenu rabbi david pardo za"l b"miktam ledavid", siman y"g: habba lomar qeriat shema beshabbat velo amar techilla "nishmat kol chay", domeh qetzat lepi sodo laqqore qeriat shema belo tepillin; ayyen sham. velaken tzarik lehizzaher bekavvanot ellu apillu hu adam pashut. gam yekavven baamirat "nishmat kol chay" lehamshik tosepet qedushshat shabbat beolam hayyetzira, ki tiqqun "nishmat kol chay" hu beseder hazzemirot shehem bitzira; vezo hakkavvana tzarik lekavven otah millebad otah shekkatabnu lekavven baamirat "nishmat kol chay" leqabbel tosepet nepesh yetera dibchinat hayyom. vetob shehaadam yirshom kol kavvanot ellu bassiddur shebbeyado, kede shettihyeh kavvanatam benaqel alayv, ki kol zeh tzarik lekavven bishlosha tebot ellu shehem "nishmat kol chay", veyaarik bahem ad sheyyashlim kol kavvanot hannizkarot bahem.

clarification.explanation: On the Sabbath a person receives an additional measure of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of the day, which is superior to that of the night. The place for receiving the additional nefesh of the day is at the saying of "Nishmat kol chai," at which point one should intend to prepare himself to receive it. He should also have in mind the two intentions given by the Ari in the words "Nishmat kol chai," which stand in place of the tefillin that are not worn on the Sabbath: (1) the initials of "Nishmat kol chai" — nun, kaf, chet — equal 78, the numerical value of three times the Name YHVH (3×26); (2) "kol chai" equals 68, the value of Ehyeh-YHVH-Ehyeh (21+26+21), which is also the numerical value of "chayim" (life). He should dwell on these three words until he has completed all the intentions in them. He should also intend, in saying "Nishmat kol chai," to draw down the additional holiness of the Sabbath into the World of Formation (Yetzirah), since "Nishmat" belongs to the Verses of Praise (Pesukei DeZimrah), which are in Yetzirah. Rabbi Michtam LeDavid wrote that one who recites the Shema on the Sabbath without having first said "Nishmat kol chai" is, according to the esoteric tradition, somewhat comparable to one who recites the Shema without tefillin. Therefore one must be careful about these intentions even as an ordinary person, and it is good to write them down in one's prayer book so they are readily available.
takeaways: On the Sabbath, an additional measure of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of the day is received, beginning with "Nishmat kol chai"
The intentions in "Nishmat kol chai" stand in place of the tefillin not worn on the Sabbath
"Nishmat kol chai" draws the additional holiness of the Sabbath into the World of Formation (Yetzirah)

The intentions: the initials of "Nishmat kol chai" = 78 = three times the Name YHVH; "kol chai" = 68 = Ehyeh-YHVH-Ehyeh = "chayim." It is good to write these down, and one should be careful about them even as an ordinary person

paragraphs: Mi sheshshakach lomar "nishmat" uberak birkat "yishtabbach" achar shirat-hayyam kemaasehu bechol - katab harab "miktam ledavid", deim nizkar qodem "bareku", akkatti zimneh hu; ayyen sham. ubesipri haqqatan "mqbtzl" heeleti: "p sheshshama haqqaddish veana "baruk Adonai hamborak", kol od shello hitchil bebirkat "yotzer or", yomar "nishmat" kede leqabbel tosepet hannepesh; ki iqqar qabbalat tosepet hannepesh bayyom hu baamirat "nishmat kol chay" velo b"bareku", veraq im hitchil birkat "yotzer or", en lo lehapsiq lomar "nishmat", ella omerah achar hattepilla belo amirat birkat "yishtabbach". mihu nireh li, deim nizkar bebirkot qeriat shema qodem shechotem "gaal yisrael", yeharher belibbo shemona tebot ellu: "nishmat kol chay tebarek et shimka Adonai elohenu", ubeet shemmeharher bahem, yeharher gam ken beqabbalat tosepet hannepesh, ki hirhur eno chashub hepseq, veyesh bo toelet qetzat leqabbel tosepet hannepesh; ukemo sheameru - hashshomea qedushsha mishshelicha tzibbur vehu betok tepillat haamida, veken kayyotze bazeh bedine berakot sheeno yakol lebarekam bepeh.

clarification.explanation: One who forgot to say "Nishmat kol chai" and recited "Yishtabach" as on weekdays: if he remembers before "Barchu," there is still time to say it. The Ben Ish Chai adds that even if he heard the Kaddish and answered "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed," as long as he has not yet begun the blessing of "Yotzer Or," he should say "Nishmat" in order to receive the additional nefesh, since the essential reception is at the saying of "Nishmat kol chai" and not at "Barchu." Only if he has already begun "Yotzer Or" should he not stop, but should say "Nishmat" after the prayer, without the blessing of "Yishtabach." And if he remembers during the blessings of the Shema, before sealing "Ga'al Yisrael," he should mentally recite the eight words "Nishmat kol chai tevarech et shimcha Adonai Eloheinu," intending in this mental recitation to receive the additional nefesh, since a mental recitation is not considered an interruption and has some benefit.
takeaways: Forgot "Nishmat" and recited "Yishtabach"; remembered before "Barchu" — there is still time
Even after "Barchu," as long as "Yotzer Or" has not begun, one should say "Nishmat"
Already began "Yotzer Or" — say it after the prayer without the blessing of "Yishtabach"
Remembered during the blessings of the Shema — mentally recite the eight words and intend to receive the additional nefesh

paragraphs: Shebach zeh d"nishmat kol chay" hu yaqar umeulleh meod, vetzarik leamero binima, vehu mesuggal al kol tzara shehaadam omed bah, sheyyiddor neder lomar achar hatztzalato mehatztzara shebach zeh shel "nishmat kol chay" veyoil lo; ukemo shekkatub beshem rabbi yehuda hechasid za"l. venizkar bitchillato neshama verucha, ki lo zaku linshama verucha ella yisrael, abal umot haolam, en lahem ella nepesh mitztzad haqqelippa; veal shebach zeh neemar (yeshaya mg,k): "am zu yatzarti li, tehillati yesapperu". venoda desod "nishmat kol chay" hu bechinat tosepet qedushshat shabbat beolam hayyetzira.

clarification.explanation: The praise "Nishmat kol chai" is precious and exceedingly excellent, and should be said in a pleasant melody. It is efficacious for any trouble a person is in — he should make a point of saying this praise after being saved from the trouble, and it will help him, as is written in the name of Rabbi Yehuda HeChasid. "Neshamah" (higher soul) and "ruach" (spirit) are mentioned at its beginning because only Israel merited neshamah and ruach, while the nations of the world have only nefesh, from the side of the kelipah; and of this praise it is said, "This people I formed for Myself; they shall declare My praise." The secret of "Nishmat kol chai" is the aspect of the additional holiness of the Sabbath in the World of Formation.
takeaways: "Nishmat kol chai" is precious and excellent, and is said in a pleasant melody
It is efficacious for any trouble; one should make a point of saying it after being saved
Neshamah and ruach are mentioned in it because only Israel merited them
Its secret is the additional holiness of the Sabbath in the World of Formation

paragraphs: Hannuscha haiqqarit hi lomar: "vah' elohim emet, lo yanum velo yishan", veken matzati beseper "chemdat-yisrael" lerabbenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l. gam tzarik lomar: "vehallebabot yirauka, vehaqqereb vehakkelayot yezammeru leshimka", kede sheyyihyeh hamminyan shalem vekannizkar b"shalme-tzibbur". veameru: "mibbiladeka en lanu goel umoshia, podeh umatztzil veoneh umerachem" - shishsha tearim, keneged berurim shel neshamot venitzotze qedushsha sheyyihyu beshishsha alapim dealema, veaach"k omer: "en lanu melek ozer vesomek ella atta" - al zeman elep hashshebii. veameru: "elohe harishonim vehaacharonim" - nireh li besiata dishmayya: "harishonim" hem haabot, shehem bechesed gebura tiperet, "vehaacharonim" - mosheh veaharon veyosep vedavid shehem benetzach hod yesod malkut. "elohha kol beriyyot" - hazzeqenim vehashshopetim vehannebiim, "veadun kol toladot" - anshe keneset haggedola, vehattenaim veamoraim, verabbanan saborae, vehaggeonim ushear chakme haddorot kullam; veayyen beresh shaar rucha haqqodesh.

clarification.explanation: The primary text to say is "And the Lord God is true; He neither slumbers nor sleeps," as found in the book Chemdat Yisrael by Rabbi Shmuel Vital. One must also say "and the hearts shall fear You, and the innermost parts and the kidneys shall sing to Your name," so that the count be complete. One says, "Besides You we have no redeemer and savior, deliverer and rescuer, answerer and merciful one" — six titles corresponding to the refinements of souls and sparks that will occur during the six thousand years of the world — and afterward, "We have no king who helps and supports but You," corresponding to the time of the seventh millennium. As for saying "God of the first and of the last": "the first" are the Patriarchs, who correspond to Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet; "the last" are Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David, who correspond to Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and Malchut. "God of all creatures" refers to the elders, judges, and prophets; "and Master of all generations" refers to the men of the Great Assembly, the Tannaim, the Amoraim, and the sages of the generations.
takeaways: The primary text: "And the Lord God is true; He neither slumbers nor sleeps"
"And the hearts shall fear You, and the innermost parts and the kidneys shall sing to Your name" is said to complete the count
Six titles correspond to the refinements of the six thousand years of the world, and "You" corresponds to the seventh millennium
"The first" are the Patriarchs, "the last" are Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David; "all creatures" and "all generations" refer to the sages of the later generations

paragraphs: "al achat meelep alpe alapim verob rabbi rebabot" - nireh li bs"d: bechakema gedola tiqqenu anshe keneset haggedola shiur zeh bealpayim urebabot; ki b"elep alpe alapim" yesh asara madregot bemispar, shehem: achadim, asarot, meot, alapim, asarot alapim, meot alapim, elep alapim, asarot alpe alapim, meot alpe alapim, elep alpe alapim; hare kan asara madregot, keneged asara sepirot vaasara hillulim sheamar david hammelek alayv hashshalom b"halluyah, hallu el beqadesho" (tehillim q"n:'); abal b"rob rabbe rebabot" yesh shelosha-asar madregot shehem: achadim, asarot, meot, alapim, rebabot, asara rebabot, mea rebabot, elep rebabot, rabbi rebabot, asara rabbi rebabot, mea rabbi rebabot, elep rabbi rebabot, rob rabbe rebabot; hare kan shelosha- asar madregot, keneged y"g mikkaylan derachame, vy"g middot, vy"g shebachim shel "yishtabbach". yomar: "yodu vibareku vishabbechu vipaaru vishoreru", keneged chamishsha bechinot haremuzim bachameshet otiyyot deshem hvy"h veqotzo shel yo"d, shehem sod nepesh rucha neshama chayya yechida. veyomar: "shavat aniyyim atta tishma" - ellu yisrael hayyoshebim baggalut; v"tzaaqat haddal" - hu mashicha ben yosep hamdoka beyissurim, kemo shenneemar (yeshaya ng,b): "vehu mechullal mippeshaenu".

clarification.explanation: With great wisdom the men of the Great Assembly instituted the formula "for one of a thousand thousand thousands, and myriads upon myriads of myriads." In the expression "a thousand thousand thousands" there are ten gradations of number, from units up to a thousand thousand thousands, corresponding to the ten sefirot and the ten praises in the psalm "Halleluyah, praise God in His sanctuary." In the expression "myriads upon myriads of myriads" there are thirteen gradations, corresponding to the thirteen attributes of mercy and the thirteen praises of "Yishtabach." One says "they shall thank, and bless, and praise, and glorify, and exalt in song" — five verbs, corresponding to the five aspects: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, and yechidah. And what is said, "the outcry of the poor You shall hear," refers to Israel dwelling in exile, while "and the cry of the destitute" refers to Mashiach ben Yosef, who is afflicted with sufferings.
takeaways: "A thousand thousand thousands" — ten gradations corresponding to the ten sefirot and the ten praises
"Myriads upon myriads of myriads" — thirteen gradations corresponding to the thirteen attributes and the praises of "Yishtabach"
Five expressions of praise correspond to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, yechidah
"The outcry of the poor" refers to Israel in exile; "the cry of the destitute" refers to Mashiach ben Yosef

paragraphs: Bebirkat "yishtabbach" yesh y"g shebachim, vehem keneged y"g mikkaylan derachame vy"g middot. veyomar otam binima ubenachat-rucha, piv velibbo shavim; veen tzarik leameram binshima achat, lekak lo yemaher baamiratam. veim hirgish sheechad hitchil beqaddish uqedushsha, yamtin, shello yatchil leameram ella ad sheyyaaneh qaddish o qedushsha, kede shello yapsiq bahem. ukebar katabti bedine "yishtabbach" beshana rishona bs"d, umah shetztzarik lehizzaher bibraka zo ubaamirat y"g shebachim hannizkarim.

clarification.explanation: In the blessing of "Yishtabach" there are thirteen praises, corresponding to the thirteen attributes of mercy. One should say them in a pleasant melody and with composure, with mouth and heart in agreement, and there is no need to say them in a single breath, so one should not rush. If he senses that someone has begun Kaddish or Kedushah, he should wait and not begin the praises until he has answered the Kaddish or Kedushah, so as not to interrupt in the middle.
takeaways: "Yishtabach" has thirteen praises, corresponding to the thirteen attributes of mercy
They are said in a pleasant melody and with composure, mouth and heart in agreement, without needing a single breath
One should wait before beginning the praises if he needs to answer Kaddish or Kedushah, so as not to interrupt

paragraphs: Birkat "yotzer or" deshabbat hu bechinat tosepet qedushshat shabbat beolam habberia, ki kol seder "yotzer" hu bibria ukemo shekkatab beshaar-hakkavvanot. veshebach "lael asher shabat" hu shebach shennizkar bo illuy hashshabbat. umah sheamar: "ubayyom hashshebii nitalla veyashab al kisse kebodo", hakkavvana: ki bechinat he" harishona deshem hvy"h baruk hu, meqannenet bibria, ubechinat va"v bitzira; vekol zeh bimot hachol, abal beyom-shabbat - bechinat va"v shebbashshem nitalla min hayyetzira veyashab al kisse kebodo bibria; velazeh amar "ubayyom hashshebii", kelomar: v' – "bayyom hashshebii nitalla veyashab al kisse kebodo", vekannizkar beshaar-hakkavvanot. vetzarik lomar: "daat utebuna sobebim hodu", veken "notenim lo kol tzeba marom"; veken tzarik lomar: "serapim vechayyot veapene haqqodesh", vekannizkar beshaar-hakkavvanot. umah sheamar: "qara leshammesh vayyizrach or", rotzeh lomar, zimmen veqiddesh, kemo: "reu qara Adonai beshem betzalel" (shemot lh, l), veken: "yisrael meqoree" (yeshaya mch, yb), kelomar, hashshemesh lo haya mazricha or lattachtonim, lule ki zimmen veqiddesh oto hashshem yitbarak lekak. veameru: "raa vehitqin tzurat hallebana" - nireh li bs"d: millat "raa", al derek mah shekkatab haramba"n za"l bappasuq (bereshit ,d): "vayyar elohim et haor ki tob", ki haratzon beqiyyum yiqqare "reiyya", shehu keinyan "veraiti ani" diqhillat (b, yg); veken "vattere haishsha ki tob haetz lemaakol", shehu keinyan sheameru (ketubbot qch): roeh ani et dibre admon, vekamohu (shemuel b tv, kz): "vayyomer hammelek el tzadoq hakkohen, haroeh atta, shuba hair beshalom"; veken kan amar "vayyar elohim et haor ki tob", sheratza beqiyyumo laad; ad kan debarayv za"l. veken hainyan kan – omer: "raa vehitqin", rotzeh lomar, chepetz veratza vehitqin tzurat hallebana, sheggazar bahem haqqiyyum vehem omedim becheptzo, sheim yitpared mehem cheptzo uretzono rega - yihyu leayin.

clarification.explanation: The blessing of "Yotzer Or" on the Sabbath is the aspect of the additional holiness of the Sabbath in the World of Creation (Beriah), since the entire order of "Yotzer" is in Beriah. The praise "to the God who rested" mentions the elevation of the Sabbath. What is said, "and on the seventh day He was exalted and sat upon His throne of glory," concerns, according to the esoteric tradition, the letter vav of the Name YHVH, which nests in Yetzirah during the weekdays but on the Sabbath is elevated from Yetzirah and sits upon the throne of glory in Beriah. One must say "knowledge and understanding surround His glory," and likewise "all the heavenly host give Him," and likewise "seraphim and the holy chayot and ofanim." What is said, "He called to the sun and it shone forth light," means He appointed and sanctified it, for the sun would not shine light for those below had the Lord not appointed and sanctified it for this. What is said, "He saw and fashioned the form of the moon," "saw" here means He desired and willed — He decreed their existence, and they stand by His will, such that if His will were to be separated from them for even a moment, they would return to nothing.
takeaways: "Yotzer Or" on the Sabbath is the aspect of the additional holiness of the Sabbath in the World of Creation (Beriah)
"On the seventh day He was exalted": the letter vav of the Name is elevated from Yetzirah to Beriah on the Sabbath
"He called to the sun" means He appointed and sanctified it to shine light
"He saw and fashioned" means He desired and willed, and the existence of creation depends on His constant will

paragraphs: Im hitchil "hammeir laaretz" bimqom "hakkol yoduka" keminhago bechol - im lo nizkar ella ad achar shehitchil "el baruk gedol dea veku'", yigmor kol alpa-beta d"l baruk veku'", veyachazor veyomar min "hakkol yoduka" al hasseder shel shabbat. vaapillu im lo nizkar ella ad achar shehitchil "lael baruk neimut", kol shello chatam adayin "baruk atta Adonai yotzer hammeorot", tzarik lachazor velomar min "hakkol yoduka" al hasseder; udelo kemi shekkatab deeno chozer lomar ella "lael asher shabat", o "el adon al kol hammaasim"; yaan ki beemet, amirat "hakkol yoduka veku'" hu tzorek gadol beshabbat, dekan nirmazim shiba hekalot dibria hanniptachim beyom-shabbat, vehem nirmazim beshishsha peamim "hakkol" hannizkarim bibraka zo, d"hakkol" leshon "hekol", veseder meqom haremez shellahem meporash beshaar-hakkavvanot; al-ken tzarik lehatchil min "hakkol yoduka". venireh li bs"d lomar od: tob lehatchil min "oseh shalom ubore et hakkol", d"p shettebot ellu yeshnam b"yotzer" dechol, ukebar amaram; mikkol maqom, meachar shehipsiq benehem baamirat "hammeir laaretz veladdarim veku'", yoter tob venakon lachazor leameram kede lechabberam im "hakkol yoduka", ki haremez shel shiba hekalot matchil min "hakkol" shel "ubore et hakkol", veacharayv remez shel "hakkol yoduka".

clarification.explanation: If, on the Sabbath, one mistakenly began "HaMe'ir la'aretz" instead of "Hakol yoducha" as on weekdays: if he does not remember until after he has already begun "El Baruch gadol de'ah," he should finish the entire alphabetical acrostic of "El Baruch" and then go back and say from "Hakol yoducha" in the Sabbath order. And even if he does not remember until after beginning "LaEl baruch ne'imot," as long as he has not yet sealed "Yotzer hame'orot," he must go back and say from "Hakol yoducha" in order. The reason is that saying "Hakol yoducha" is a great necessity on the Sabbath, since it alludes to the seven palaces of Beriah that are opened on the Sabbath, alluded to by the six occurrences of the word "hakol" in the blessing, since "hakol" is a term related to "heichal" (palace). It is also good to begin from "Oseh shalom uvorei et hakol," in order to connect it with "Hakol yoducha," since the allusion to the seven palaces begins from the "hakol" of "uvorei et hakol."
takeaways: Mistakenly began "HaMe'ir la'aretz" instead of "Hakol yoducha" — finish the alphabetical acrostic and go back to "Hakol yoducha"
As long as "Yotzer hame'orot" has not been sealed, one goes back to say "Hakol yoducha" in the Sabbath order
"Hakol yoducha" is a great necessity on the Sabbath, alluding to the seven palaces of Beriah through six occurrences of "hakol"
It is good to begin from "Oseh shalom uvorei et hakol," to connect it with "Hakol yoducha"

paragraphs: Heka deamar yotzer dechol, velo nizkar ella ad shechatam habberaka d"yotzer hammeorot", eno chozer lomar hasseder shel shabbat, ella gomer birkat "ahabat olam"; veayyen "shalme-tzibbur", dap k"ch; yeuyyan sham. venireh li deyachazor lomar kol seder hayyotzer deshabbat behirhur halleb, vegam habberakot yeharher balleb; vekol shehu behirhur, yesh bo toelet, veen bo din hepseq velo beraka lebattala, ukemo shekkatabti bimqomot acherim.

clarification.explanation: If one said the weekday "Yotzer" and did not remember until after sealing the blessing "Yotzer hame'orot," he does not go back to say the Sabbath order, but finishes the blessing of "Ahavat olam." It seems to the Ben Ish Chai that he should go back and say the entire Sabbath "Yotzer" order mentally, and also recite the blessings mentally, since anything done mentally has some benefit, and it involves no law of interruption nor a blessing said in vain.
takeaways: Said the weekday "Yotzer" and sealed "Yotzer hame'orot" — does not go back, but finishes "Ahavat olam"
It seems that he should go back and say the Sabbath "Yotzer" order mentally
A mental recitation has benefit, and involves no interruption or blessing in vain

paragraphs: Gam beshabbat tzarik lismok geulla litpilla, velo yapsiq apillu leqaddish uqedushsha ubareku; veyizzaher shello yiteh lehitpallel shel chol; veim taa, yidag kol oto shabua vipashpesh bemaasayv. veim taa vehitpallel tepillat chol venizkar beemtza habberaka, yigmor otah beraka shettaa bah, veaach"k chozer leshel shabbat. veim haya sabur shehu chol, vehitchil addata dechol, umiyyad kesheamar tebat "atta" nizkar qodem sheamar tebat "chonen" - hava lah "hitchil beshel chol" im hu bitpillat shacharit sheenah matchelet b"atta"; abal im hu bitpillat arbit umincha shemmatchilim b"atta", eno gomer "atta chonen", ella mesayyem beshel shabbat, kevan shennizkar qodem sheamar tebat "chonen"; abal im haya yodea vezoker shehu shabbat, veshello bekavvana hitchil tebat "atta", apillu im hu bitpillat shacharit sheenah potachat b"atta" - eno gomer "atta chonen", dechashebinan leh ketaa bitpillat shabbat ben zo lezo, shehare yakol lomar "atta qiddashta" o "atta echad", velaken atta yomar tekep "yismach mosheh". ushelicha-tzibbur shettaa bachazara vehitchil beshel chol venizkar, eno gomer habberaka shel chol, ella poseq umatchil beshel shabbat; ki din zeh lo neemar ella bitpillat lachash velo bitpillat hachazara.

clarification.explanation: On the Sabbath too one must juxtapose redemption to prayer, and should not interrupt between "Ga'al Yisrael" and the Amidah even for Kaddish, Kedushah, or Barchu. One should be careful not to mistakenly pray the weekday prayer, and if he errs he should be troubled about it for that entire week and examine his deeds. If he erred and began the weekday prayer and remembered in the middle of a blessing, he should finish that blessing and then return to the Sabbath text. If he thought it was a weekday and began "Atah" ("You"), and immediately upon saying "Atah" he remembered before saying "Chonen" ("gracious"): in the morning prayer, which does not begin with "Atah," this is considered as though he had begun the weekday text; but in the evening and afternoon prayers, which do begin with "Atah," he does not finish "Atah chonen," but concludes with the Sabbath text. But if he knew it was the Sabbath and only unintentionally began with "Atah," even in the morning prayer he does not finish "Atah chonen," since this is considered a mistake between one Sabbath prayer and another Sabbath prayer, and he should immediately say "Yismach Moshe." A prayer leader who erred in the repetition and began the weekday text and then remembered does not finish the weekday blessing, but stops and begins the Sabbath text, since the law of finishing the blessing applies only to the silent Amidah.
takeaways: On the Sabbath too, redemption is juxtaposed to prayer, without interruption even for Kaddish or Kedushah
Erring into the weekday prayer mid-blessing — finish that blessing, then return to the Sabbath text
Remembered right after "Atah," before "Chonen": in the morning it counts as having begun the weekday text; in the evening and afternoon, conclude with the Sabbath text
A prayer leader who errs in the repetition stops immediately and does not finish the weekday blessing

paragraphs: Taa vehitpallel shel chol beshabbat velo hizkir shel shabbat: im higgia l"oseh shalom", "p shello aqar raglayv chozer larosh; veim lo higgia l"oseh shalom", "p shessiyyem tepillato, eno chozer ella leshel shabbat. veim taa vehitpallel shel chol velo nizkar ella ad achar shehitpallel musap, "p deyesh mi shekkatab sheeno chozer lehitpallel shacharit shel shabbat, mikkol maqom hannakon hu deyitpallel mincha shettayim kedin mi sheshshakach lehazkir rosh chodesh beshacharit venizkar achar musap, sheppasaq harashba" za"l deyitpallel mincha shettayim, vekannizkar beseper "shiyyure-beraka". veayyen "bet-menucha", ot d'; yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: One who erred and prayed the weekday Amidah on the Sabbath without mentioning the Sabbath at all: if he reached "Oseh shalom," even without having moved his feet, he goes back to the beginning of the prayer. If he did not reach "Oseh shalom," even though he finished the blessing, he does not go back further than the Sabbath prayer. If he erred and prayed the weekday text and did not remember until after praying the Musaf (additional) prayer, even though some have written that he need not go back, the correct ruling is that he should pray the afternoon prayer (Minchah) twice, like the law of one who forgot to mention Rosh Chodesh in the morning prayer and remembered after Musaf, which the Rashba ruled should be remedied by praying Minchah twice.
takeaways: Erred into the weekday prayer on the Sabbath, reached "Oseh shalom" — goes back to the beginning
Did not reach "Oseh shalom" — goes back only to the Sabbath prayer, even having finished the blessing
Did not remember until after Musaf — should pray Minchah twice, as with forgetting Rosh Chodesh

paragraphs: Im belel-shabbat hitpallel shel yom chol bilbad velo hizkir shabbat: im shama mishshelicha-tzibbur beraka meen sheba merosh vead sop, yatza, veim lav, chozer umitpallel; velaken shelicha-tzibbur atzmo shettaa belachash shello, yotze yede choba bibraka meen sheba. veim haadam mistappeq im taa vehitpallel shel chol im lav, eno chozer lehitpallel, deamerinan, missetama hitpallel shel shabbat, ki chamero shel yom gorem derame annapsheh beet tepilla, umiddekar lehitpallel tepillat shabbat.

clarification.explanation: If, on Sabbath night, one prayed only the weekday text without mentioning the Sabbath: if he heard from the prayer leader the blessing of "Mei'ein Sheva" ("Magen Avot") from beginning to end, he has fulfilled his obligation; if not, he must pray again. Therefore even the prayer leader himself, who erred in his own silent Amidah, fulfills his obligation through the blessing of "Mei'ein Sheva." And if a person is in doubt whether he erred and prayed the weekday text, he does not pray again, since it is assumed that he prayed the Sabbath text, because the special character of the day causes a person to be attentive during the prayer and remember to pray the Sabbath prayer.
takeaways: Prayed the weekday text on Sabbath night, but heard "Mei'ein Sheva" in full from the prayer leader — has fulfilled his obligation
The prayer leader himself, if he erred in his silent Amidah, is exempted through "Mei'ein Sheva"
One who is in doubt whether he erred does not pray again, since the special character of the day is assumed to have kept him attentive

paragraphs: Kesheomed lehitpallel shacharit - achar sheomer pasuq "adonay sepatay tiptach, upi yaggid tehillateka" - yekavven leqabbel tosepet harucha shel bechinat hayyom, vikavven leqabbel zeh qodem sheyyatchil bebirkat "abot", ukemo shekkatab beshaar-hakkavvanot. vekatabti besipri haqqadosh "mqbtzl", sheim shakach lekavven kavvana hannizkar shel qabbalat tosepet harucha, yesh lo taqqana lekavven otah bitchillat tepillat musap, achar sheyyomar pasuq "adonay sepatay tiptach veku'".

clarification.explanation: When one is about to pray the morning prayer, after saying "O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall declare Your praise," he should intend to receive the additional ruach of the aspect of the day, and should have this intention before beginning the blessing of "Avot." One who forgot to have this intention of receiving the additional ruach has a remedy: he can have this intention at the beginning of the Musaf prayer, after saying "O Lord, open my lips."
takeaways: In the morning prayer, after "O Lord, open my lips," one intends to receive the additional ruach of the day
The reception should occur before beginning the blessing of "Avot"
One who forgot may intend it at the beginning of Musaf, after "O Lord, open my lips"

paragraphs: Baamida shel shacharit deshabbat kesheomerim "chemdat yamim oto qarata" - en mesayyemim "zeker lemaaseh bereshit", veraq bearbit umusap omerim "zeker lemaaseh bereshit". ubeseper "mishnat-chasidim" natan taam lazeh "p hassod, ak bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l lo nimtza taam meporash al zeh.

clarification.explanation: In the Sabbath morning Amidah, when saying "the most cherished of days You have called it," one does not conclude with "in remembrance of the work of Creation"; only in the evening and Musaf prayers is "in remembrance of the work of Creation" said. The book Mishnat Chasidim gave a reason for this according to the esoteric tradition, but no explicit reason for it is found in the words of the Ari.
takeaways: In the Sabbath morning prayer, "in remembrance of the work of Creation" is not said after "the most cherished of days"
It is said in the evening and Musaf prayers
Mishnat Chasidim gave a kabbalistic reason; no explicit reason is found in the Ari

paragraphs: Beshabbat omer hachazzan qodem hotzaat seper tora: "atta hareeta ladaat veku'", vehem shemona pesuqim, keneged shiba haolim leseper tora vehammaptir; ubeyom tob medallegin b' pesuqim, umatchilin min "yehi Adonai elohenu immanu"; ubechol omer shelosha pesuqim bilbad, keneged sheloshet haolim vekannizkar b"shalme-tzibbur"; vehammosipin vegorein, en lahem al mah sheyyismoku. vetzarik kol adam lomar "berik shemeh demare alema" beet hotzaat seper hattora min hahekol - ben beshabbat, ben beyom tob, ben beyom hakkippurim. ub"kisse-eliyyahu" katub sheyyomar oto gam berosh chodesh, mippene sheggam berosh chodesh omerim "keter" biqdushshat musap, velaken matze lememar nussach hannizkar: "berik kitreka veatrak", mishsheen ken bechol, en taam leamero.

clarification.explanation: On the Sabbath, before taking out the Torah scroll, the cantor says "Atah hor'eita lada'at" — eight verses, corresponding to the seven who are called up plus the Maftir. On a festival, two verses are skipped and it begins from "Yehi Adonai Eloheinu imanu," and on a weekday only three verses are said, corresponding to the three who are called up. Those who add to or subtract from this have nothing to rely on. Every person must say "Berich shemei demarei alma" at the time the Torah scroll is taken out of the ark, whether on the Sabbath, a festival, or Yom Kippur. In Kisei Eliyahu it is written that it should also be said on Rosh Chodesh, since "Keter" is also said in the Kedushah of Musaf on that day, and it is therefore relevant to say the formula "Berich kitrach ve'atrach" — unlike on a weekday, where there is no reason to say it.
takeaways: On the Sabbath, "Atah hor'eita lada'at" is said — eight verses corresponding to the seven called up plus the Maftir
On a festival, two verses are skipped; on a weekday, only three verses are said, corresponding to the three called up
"Berich shemei demarei alma" is said when the Torah scroll is taken out, on the Sabbath, a festival, and Yom Kippur
On Rosh Chodesh it is also said, because of "Keter"; on a weekday there is no reason to say it

paragraphs: Keshemmotziin seper tora min hahekol, potechin oto umarin oto lekol haqqahal. vetzarik shekkullam yishtachavu leseper tora keshehu patucha, apillu nashim vetap, veyomru "vezot hattora veku'", "el shadday emet, mosheh emet vetorato emet"; vehattaam: ki hattora nittena lanu meolam habberia, sheshsham meir "el shadday", vesham sod habbina shehu sod shem "ehyeh" shemmisseparo k", vk" peamim hy"h oleh mispar "emet"; velaken mosheh shennatena tora al yado veniqret al shemo, hinneh mispar shemo oleh "el shadday". veim haadam omed bemaqom sheeno yakol lehapsiq bedibbur, yishtachaveh bilbad. veraiti beseper echad shekkatub sham: tob sheyyistakkel haadam batteba, sheyyehe ot rishon shellah kemo ot rishon shebbissemo; umatzati katub shebbeshabbat beshacharit yishtachaveh leseper tora shiba hishtachavayot keneged haolin, veken kol zeman, yihyu hishtachavayot keneged haolin leseper tora, venakon hu.

Vehinneh beshaar-hakkavvanot meporash minhago shel rabbenu haari"y za"l behotzaat seper tora kak hu: menashsheq hasseper tora, umelavvehu laleket acharayv keshemmolikin oto min hahekol el hatteba liqrot bo. veaach"k haya nishar sham samuk el hatteba ad sheyyihyu potechin et hasseper tora umarin oto laqqahal; veaz haya mistakkel beotiyyot hasseper tora mammash, vehaya omer sheal yede histakkelut haadam miqqarob kol kak sheyyukal liqro haotiyyot heteb, al yede zeh nimshak or gadol el haadam. veaach"k haya chozer limqomo harishon veyosheb sham meyushshab ad siyyum qeriat happarasha, velo keotam hannohagim laamod biqriat hasseper tora, ad kan; yeuyyan sham. upoh irenu bagdad nohagin liptoach hasseper tora leharoto laqqahal beet shemmotzio min haargaz shebbakkotel betok hahekol; upeticha zo enah niret lekol haqqahal. veaach"k molikin hasseper tora latteba asher beemtza bet-hakkeneset, upotechin oto laqqahal bearba ruchot hatteba shene peamim bezo achar zo. veaach"k mannichim oto al hakkisse shebberosh hatteba liqrot bo. veachar sheggomerin haqqeria sogerin hattiq, veen potechin oto leharoto laqqahal beet shemmolikin oto min hatteba lahekol keminhag meqomot acherim shezzakar mvr"m za"l behaggahat hashshulchan. vaani amarti: minhag irenu shello liptoach paam shenit hasseper tora keshemmachazirin oto lahekol hu minhag yapeh umetuqqan al pi hassod; yaan ki meporash bedibre rabbenu za"l beshaar-hakkavvanot, diptichat hasseper tora hu, sheyyitgalleh hearat hattora hakketuba betoko lachutz el kol haqqahal; veaach"k beet sheqqorin battora, az yotze haor shebbetoko lachutz, shehu hattora atzmah shenniqret "or". vekatab od sham achar zeh vezeh leshono: vehinneh heara zo enah nisheret kak raq lepi shaa, veaach"k chozerin mitallemim bipnim kammatchila; velaken tekep achar haqqeria sogerin hasseper tora umachazirin oto limqomo tok hahekol; ad kan leshono. ulepi zeh nireh minhag irenu nakon, shessogerin oto tekep achar haqqeria, vetu en taam lepitcho achar sheasu bisgira remez lehitallemut haorot bipnim.

clarification.explanation: When the Torah scroll is taken from the ark, it is opened and shown to the whole congregation, and everyone must bow to the open Torah scroll, even women and children, and say "Vezot haTorah," "El Shaddai emet, Moshe emet vetorato emet." The reason: the Torah was given to us from the World of Creation (Beriah), in which the Name "El Shaddai" and the secret of Binah shine, and the numerical value of "Moshe" equals "El Shaddai." One who is standing where he cannot interrupt with speech should only bow. On Sabbath morning it is customary to bow to the Torah scroll seven times, corresponding to the seven who are called up. The custom of the Ari was to kiss the Torah scroll and accompany it, and afterward to look closely at the actual letters while it is opened and shown to the congregation, since by looking closely, to the point of being able to read the letters, a great light is drawn to the person; he then returns to his place and sits until the reading is finished. In Baghdad the custom is to open and show the Torah scroll to the congregation when it is taken out, opening it on the reading table to the four directions, but it is not opened again when it is returned to the ark. This custom is fitting according to the esoteric tradition, since opening the Torah scroll reveals the illumination of the Torah to the congregation, and during the reading the light goes outward, but this illumination remains only temporarily and then withdraws and disappears again; therefore, immediately after the reading, the Torah scroll is closed and returned, and there is no reason to open it again.
takeaways: The open Torah scroll is shown to the congregation and everyone bows, even women and children
The numerical value of "Moshe" equals "El Shaddai," and the Torah is from the World of Creation
The Ari's custom was to look closely at the letters, since this draws down great light
Baghdad custom: it is not opened again when returned to the ark, since the illumination is only temporary

paragraphs: Beshabbat olin leseper tora shiba chutz min hammaptir, vehem keneged chesed gebura tiperet netzach hod yesod malkut (chg"t nhy"m). vezeh seder maalatam al pi hassod: hashshishshi gadol mikkullam, shehu keneged hayyesod; vehashsheni lo bemaala hu hashshelishi, shehu keneged tiperet; vehashshelishi bemaala, hakkohen, shehu keneged chesed; veacharayv hallevi, shehu keneged gebura; veacharayv d', shehu keneged netzach; veacharayv hachamishi, shehu keneged hod; veacharayv hashshebii, shehu keneged malkut; velaken "qatan oleh leminyan shiba" (megilla kg.) - shebii davqa. ubemincha shabbat qorin shelosha, keneged chakema bina daat; ubeyom tob chamishsha: harishon keneged netzach dechakema, vehashsheni neged netzach debina, vehashshelishi - hod dechakema, veharebii - hod debina, vehachamishi - yesod dechakema, vekannizkar beshaar-hakkavvanot. ulepi zeh, beyom tob - hachamishi gadol mikkullam. vekatebu happoseqim siman lishlosha deminchat shabbat vesheni vachamishi - pasuq "yebarekka Adonai veyishmereka", shehu shelosha tebot; vesiman laolim beyom tob shehem chamishsha - pasuq "yaer Adonai vego'"; vesiman laolim beshacharit deshabbat – "yissa Adonai panayv vego'". vn"l shessiman laolim shel yom hakkippurim shehem shishsha – pasuq: "vesamu et shemi al bene-yisrael", dead kan nishlam hatztzivvuy, vetebot "vaani abarekem" enam biklal hatztzivvuy. veod, kevan deyesh etnach betebat "yisrael", hare nishlam kan happasuq, dekol etnach nechshab sop pasuq kannoda.

clarification.explanation: On the Sabbath, seven people are called up to the Torah besides the Maftir, corresponding to Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malchut. The order of their rank according to the esoteric tradition: the sixth is the greatest of all, corresponding to Yesod; after him the third, corresponding to Tiferet; after him the Kohen, corresponding to Chesed; after him the Levite, corresponding to Gevurah; after him the fourth, corresponding to Netzach; after him the fifth, corresponding to Hod; and after him the seventh, corresponding to Malchut. Therefore "a minor may be counted among the seven" specifically as the seventh. At the Sabbath afternoon service three are called up, corresponding to Chochmah, Binah, Da'at, and on a festival, five. The halachic authorities gave mnemonics: for the three of the Sabbath afternoon service, and for the second and fifth aliyot, the verse "May the Lord bless you and keep you," which has three words; for the five of a festival, "Ya'er Adonai" (may the Lord shine); and for the seven of the Sabbath morning service, "Yisa Adonai panav" (may the Lord lift up His face). The mnemonic for the six who are called up on Yom Kippur is "Vesamu et shemi al benei Yisrael."
takeaways: On the Sabbath, seven are called up, corresponding to Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferet-Netzach-Hod-Yesod-Malchut
The sixth is the greatest, corresponding to Yesod; a minor may be counted specifically as the seventh
At Sabbath Minchah, three are called up, corresponding to Chochmah-Binah-Da'at; on a festival, five
Mnemonics based on the number of words in verses from the Priestly Blessing help remember the count for each occasion

paragraphs: Haoleh leseper tora yireh techilla meqom haqqeria, veyistakkel bappasuq harishon sheatid liqrot, veaach"k yekasseh hakketab al-yede mappa vibarek birkat hattora, veyasir hammappa veyiqra; veachar sheggamar yachazor vikasseh hakketab bammappa vibarek beraka acharona; veyizzaher beet shemmebarek, leechoz beseper tora atzmo "y hammappa velo battiq. veyannicha shette yadayv beet habberaka, achat mitztzad zeh veachat mitztzad zeh, vikavven liklol hassemol beyamin; veachar sheggomer habberaka shellepaneha, mesir yad hassemol, veyishshaer ochez beyad yamin bilbad "y mappa, ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l kol zeh beshaar-hakkavvanot. vekatab sham morenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l, deen chiyyub leechoz hasseper tora bemitpachat, ella raq beet qeriat hattora betzibbur, sheaz mitgallim haorot haelyonim kaamur, abal shello bishat qeriat seper tora, kegon shetztzarik letaqqeno, o sheochazo letzorek acher, en kan chiyyub leechoz bo "y hammitpachat; yeuyyan sham. venireh li: beshaa shehu poteach hasseper tora leharot hakketab laqqahal veroeh sheeno patucha beotah parasha sheqqorin bah, vetzarik liglol bo shenayim o shelosha dappim, detzarik lizzaher leechoz "y hammitpachat gam lepi daat morenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l, yaan ki meporash bedibre rabbenu za"l, dibet sheppoteach hasseper tora bahekol kede liqrot - mittaglit hearat hattora hakketuba betoko lachutz el kol haqqahal, besod beqia hashshenit kannizkar' beshaar-hakkavvanot; velaken tzarik lehizzaher bazeh meotah shaa; veken yizzaher hashlicha-tzibbur beet sheqqore bo betzibbur venishlam haddap sheppatucha lepanayv, shetztzarik limshok hayyeria middap laddap ad siyyum happarasha, detzarik lehizzaher sheyyochaz bayyeria "y hammitpachat.

clarification.explanation: One called up to the Torah should first look at the place of the reading and glance at the first verse he will read, then cover the text with the cloth and recite the blessing over the Torah, remove the cloth, and read; after finishing, he should cover it again and recite the final blessing. He should be careful, during the blessing, to hold the Torah scroll itself through the cloth, not the case, and should place both hands on it — one on each side — intending to include the left within the right; after the first blessing he should remove the left hand and remain holding with the right hand alone, through the cloth (the Ari, Sha'ar HaKavanot). Rabbi Shmuel Vital wrote that there is no obligation to hold the scroll with a cloth except during the actual public reading of the Torah (when the supernal lights are revealed), but not when it is not the time of reading (such as when arranging it) there is no such obligation. It seems to the Ben Ish Chai that even according to Rabbi Shmuel Vital one must hold it with the cloth already at the moment the scroll is opened to show the text to the congregation and several pages must be rolled — since at the moment of opening in the ark for the reading, the illumination of the Torah is revealed to the congregation (the secret of the "second splitting"); and likewise the prayer leader, when he finishes the open page and must draw the parchment from page to page, should hold the parchment through the cloth.
takeaways: One called up: looks at the reading place, covers with the cloth and blesses, uncovers and reads, then covers and recites the final blessing; holds the scroll itself (not the case) with both hands, removing the left after the first blessing

Holding the scroll with a cloth is required during the actual reading (the secret of the "second splitting") — for Rabbi Yosef Chaim, also when opening the scroll to show the congregation and when turning pages

paragraphs: Im hu beemtza qeriat shema uqerauhu laalot leseper tora, apillu sheqqerauhu bishmo - lo yaaleh, ella davqa im yodea beatzmo sheyyukal ligmor haqriat shema bederek hilluko ad sheyyaggia etzel hasseper tora. veim hu omed bebirkot qeriat shema uqerauhu bishmo - heeleti besipri haqqadosh "rab-pealim" bitshuba, bs"d, sheyyukal laalot; veasiti kamma sapeq sepeqot, vekullam mithappekim.

clarification.explanation: If one is in the middle of reciting the Shema and is called up to the Torah, even by his name, he should not go up, unless he knows he can finish the Shema while walking to the Torah scroll. But if he is in the blessings of the Shema and is called by his name, the Ben Ish Chai, in his book Rav Pe'alim, ruled that he may go up, after weighing several considerations that offset each other.
takeaways: In the middle of the Shema and called up — should not go up unless he can finish while walking
In the blessings of the Shema and called by name — he may go up

paragraphs: Haoleh leseper tora, lo yismok atzmo al haammud o al kisse hatteba, veken hachazzan haqqore yizzaher bekak. ubazzeman hazzeh denohagim dehachazzan hu haqqore, yizzaher haola liqrot im hachazzan belachash shello yashmia leazenayv. vehaoleh omer qodem habberaka: "bareku et Adonai hamborak", vehaqqahal onin: "baruk Adonai veku'". upoh irenu nohagim lomar: "rabbanan, bareku et Adonai hamborak". vikavven bibraka acharona "asher natan lanu torat emet" - zo tora shebbiktab, "vechayye olam nata betokenu" - zo tora shebbeal peh. veyishtaddel haadam laalot leseper tora lepachot paam achat bechodesh. vekol haola leseper tora, yaaleh bederek qetzara, veyered bederek arukka. veasur leadam latzet ulehannicha hasseper tora patucha, apillu ben gabra legabra; umittok dochaq, shari ben gabra legabra. veim qorin leadam sheshshomea qeriat seper tora bebet-hakkeneset zo, kede sheyyelek veyaaleh leseper tora acheret bebet-hakkeneset acheret, muttar latzet apillu beemtza haqqeria, kevan degam hu holek liqrot battora; vekol shekken heka dehatztzibbur shel bet hakkeneset haacheret mamtinim alayv labo.

clarification.explanation: One called up to the Torah should not lean on the reading stand or on the chair by the ark, and likewise the cantor who reads. Nowadays, since the cantor is the one reading, the one called up should be careful to read along with the cantor quietly, without letting his own voice be heard. The one called up says, before the blessing, "Bless the Lord who is blessed," and the congregation answers; in Baghdad the custom is to say "Rabbanan, bless the Lord who is blessed." In the final blessing, he should intend "who has given us a Torah of truth" as referring to the Written Torah, and "and has planted eternal life within us" as referring to the Oral Torah. One should make an effort to be called up to the Torah at least once a month. Everyone called up should go up by the shorter route and come down by the longer route. It is forbidden to leave the Torah scroll open and unattended, and this is permitted only in a case of pressing need, between one aliyah and the next. If someone hearing the reading in this synagogue is called to go up in another synagogue, he may leave even in the middle of the reading, since he too is going to read from the Torah.
takeaways: The one called up and the reader should not lean; nowadays the one called up reads quietly along with the cantor
He intends "a Torah of truth" for the Written Torah, and "eternal life" for the Oral Torah
He goes up by the shorter route and down by the longer route, and should be called up at least once a month
The Torah scroll should not be left open unattended, except in pressing need between aliyot

paragraphs: Abel betok shenem asar chodesh al ab veem, toil aliyyat habben lemaptir yoter tob mealiyyat hammashlim; vekol shekken im hu maptir beqarebbenot hammusapim; vekol shekken im hu maptir dezakor upara, deyesh omerim shehem deorayeta.

clarification.explanation: For a mourner within twelve months for his father or mother, the son's aliyah as Maftir is more beneficial for the elevation of the deceased's soul than the aliyah of the one completing the reading (the seventh). This is all the more so if he is the Maftir for the Torah portion of the additional offerings (Musafim), and even more so if he is the Maftir for the special portion of Zachor or Parah, which some say are read as a Torah obligation.
takeaways: A mourner within twelve months benefits more from the Maftir aliyah than from the seventh (completing) aliyah
It is preferable to be Maftir for the portion of the additional offerings
It is even more preferable to be Maftir for Zachor or Parah, which some consider a Torah obligation

paragraphs: Achar qeriat-hattora yitpallelu musap; veyomru nosach "tikkanta" shehu meyussad al alpa-beta beseder tashra"q, ubesopo chamishsha tebot beseder mntzp"k. veyesh siddurim shennidpas bahem debarim yeterim al chamishsha otiyyot dmntzp"k, veen rauy leameram, deen bazeh taam.

clarification.explanation: After the Torah reading, the Musaf prayer is prayed, and the formula "Tikanta Shabbat" is said, which is built on the reverse order of the alphabet (Tav-Shin-Reish-Kof, etc.), ending with five words in the order of the letters Mem-Nun-Tzadi-Peh-Kaf (the five letters with final forms). Some printed prayer books have additions beyond these five letters, and it is not proper to say them, since they have no reason behind them.
takeaways: Musaf is prayed and "Tikanta Shabbat" is said, built on the reverse alphabet
It ends with five words in the order of the final letters Mem-Nun-Tzadi-Peh-Kaf
Additions printed beyond this should not be said, as they have no basis

paragraphs: Bachazara betzibbur yomar qedushshat "keter"; ukesheomer hachazzan tebat "ayyeh", yaarik bah harbeh, kede shekkol adam yekavven otah shaa leqabbel tosepet neshama shel bechinat hayyom; veqabbala zo tzerika lihyot betebat "ayyeh" davqa, laken tzarik hashlicha tzibbur lehaarik bah beniggun. veim haadam odennu baamida belachash, veshama sheshshelicha tzibbur omer qedushsha, yishtoq veyishma vikavven behirhur halleb beqabbalat tosepet neshama betebat "ayyeh". ukesheyyomar pasuq "shema yisrael" biqdushshat musap, yekavven leqabbel alayv limsor atzmo al qiddush-hashshem; veashre hazzokeh laasot qabbala zo beemet ubetamim, vealayv tabo birkat tob.

clarification.explanation: In the congregational repetition of Musaf, the Kedushah of "Keter" is said. When the cantor says the word "Ayeh" ("where is He"), he should draw it out at length in melody, so that everyone can, at that moment, intend to receive the additional neshamah of the aspect of the day, since this reception must occur specifically at the word "Ayeh." If a person is still in the silent Amidah and hears the prayer leader saying the Kedushah, he should be silent, listen, and intend, mentally, to receive the additional neshamah at the word "Ayeh." When he says "Shema Yisrael" in the Kedushah of Musaf, he should intend to accept upon himself self-sacrifice for the sanctification of God's name, and fortunate is the one who merits to fulfill this acceptance truly and wholeheartedly.
